# Spoken 0.2.11 — Test Build 25
A reliability release for meetings: Apple's echo reduction is always on, a meeting keeps recording when you switch microphones or headphones, and every overlay menu works over fullscreen apps.
## Meetings
- **Echo reduction is always on.** Meeting recordings use Apple's own voice processing, the same as FaceTime, so a call played through speakers no longer ends up twice in the transcript. Other apps may play slightly quieter while you record. - **Switching devices never stops a meeting.** Connecting AirPods, unplugging headphones or a call app changing the device no longer ends the recording. If the microphone you chose disappears, Spoken uses the Mac's microphone and switches back when yours returns. A short note in the overlay says which microphone is in use. - **Faster start.** Starting the first meeting after launch no longer pauses for several seconds. - **Calmer notch.** The recording capsule at the notch no longer flickers when the pointer rests at its edge, and its rounded corners stay intact. - **Menus over fullscreen apps.** The "…" menu, the system audio menu, the calendar choice and the speaker review menu open while another app is in fullscreen. The project can be changed in the meeting start window. - **Progress beside the bell.** Transcription, speaker detection and flows of your meetings show their progress in one place next to the bell, including speaker proposals waiting for your decision. - **Correct speakers faster.** Change the speaker of one passage or of all passages of that speaker at once, with Undo. - **Delete Audio keeps the transcript.** Removing a meeting's audio frees space but keeps transcript, speakers and notes.
## Reading long transcripts
- Scrolling long meetings is smooth. - While playing, you can scroll freely; after a short pause the transcript follows the playback again. Pausing no longer jumps back, and a click in the timeline brings the transcript to that position.
## App
- **Menu bar only.** Closing the window leaves Spoken in the menu bar; Quit asks first. - **Agent approvals** arrive as a macOS notification instead of a modal window. Each agent capability can be Off, Ask or Automatic. - **Calendar** shows when it is not connected and can be disconnected. - **First launch** has a simpler setup wizard.
## Update an existing installation
In **Spoken**, choose **Check for Updates…**. Download and install the update, then allow Spoken to restart. The installed version should be **0.2.11 (25)**. Finish any recording or dictation first.
The library format is unchanged. Builds 9 and newer can receive this update.

# Spoken 0.2.10 — Test Build 24
The first test build signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple. From the next update on, macOS keeps Spoken's permissions and keychain access. Agents can now change your library after your approval, and floating panels are easier to read without a notch.
## Changes
- **Signed and notarized.** macOS opens Spoken without "Open Anyway" and recognises later updates as the same app, so Microphone, Screen & System Audio Recording, Accessibility and keychain access stay allowed. - **Keychain.** API keys and agent connection keys are stored under "Spoken". Existing keys move over by themselves. - **Agents can change the library.** Through the MCP tool `library.apply` an agent can create projects, rename projects and meetings, update the About text, move meetings and move items to or from the Trash. Spoken shows the whole batch once for your approval and applies all of it or nothing. Nothing can be deleted permanently, and an agent cannot empty the Trash. - **Agent permissions.** Settings › Agents has one switch "Allow library changes" with a checkbox per kind of change. Earlier grants carry over. - **Readable floating panels.** Without a notch, for example on an external display, panels use tinted Liquid Glass. Buttons, the speaker name field and "Verwerfen" share one clear style. - **Calendar.** Settings › Meetings › Calendar can disconnect the calendar. The macOS permission itself is removed in System Settings. - **Smaller agent footprint.** Spoken's MCP connection loads about 1,800 tokens.
## Update an existing installation
In **Spoken**, choose **Check for Updates…**. Download and install the update, then allow Spoken to restart. The installed version should be **0.2.10 (24)**. Finish any recording or dictation first.
### One last time: allow permissions again
This update changes Spoken's signature from ad-hoc to Developer ID, so macOS treats it as a new app once more:
- **macOS asks again** for Microphone, Screen & System Audio Recording, Accessibility or Calendar: allow it. - **Keychain asks** whether Spoken may use its saved keys: choose **Always Allow**. - **Dictation records nothing, text is not inserted, or system audio is silent**, although Spoken is listed as allowed: open **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, select the affected section, remove **Spoken** with "–", then open Spoken and allow it again. Spoken › Settings › Permissions shows which permission is missing.
Later updates keep these permissions.
The library format is unchanged. Builds 9 and newer can receive this update.
## Fresh installation
Download the DMG, drag **Spoken** to **Applications**, eject the DMG, then open Spoken from Applications. This is the release app, not Spoken Dev. The test target is an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 15 or newer. The DMG is signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple.
## Validation and limitations
The automated regression suite, the signature and notarization of the exact DMG are checked before publication. The new library changes, agent permissions, calendar disconnect and floating panels are covered by automated tests but were not yet tried by hand in the running app. The agent approval is still a plain macOS dialog (KON-247). Known open items: Outlook calendars (KON-270), Spoken in Claude Desktop and Cowork (KON-269), and Models & Providers clipping in a narrow window (KON-256). The Spoken Library remains local and unencrypted.

# Spoken 0.2.9 — Test Build 23
A small fix release: MP4 recordings can be imported, outdated models are reported, and agents use far less context through Spoken's MCP server.
## Changes
- **MP4 import.** MP4 files (for example Teams or Zoom recordings) can be imported as meeting audio. Spoken uses only the audio track. - **Outdated models.** When a connection no longer offers a chosen model, dictation modes and text workflows say "Model … is not offered" with Choose Model, and the bell lists it. - **Agents.** The Spoken MCP server answers in smaller parts: short connection instructions, long texts in parts of about 8,000 characters, and shorter default lists.
## Update an existing installation
In **Spoken**, choose **Check for Updates…**. Download and install the update, then allow Spoken to restart. The installed version should be **0.2.9 (23)**. Finish any recording or dictation first.
### If something stops working after the update
This test build is ad-hoc signed, like the earlier ones. macOS ties privacy permissions to an app's signature, so after an update it can treat Spoken as a new app:
- **macOS asks again** for Microphone, Screen & System Audio Recording, Accessibility or Calendar: allow it. - **Dictation records nothing, text is not inserted, or system audio is silent**, although Spoken is still listed as allowed: open **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, select the affected section (Microphone, Screen & System Audio Recording, Accessibility), remove **Spoken** with "–", then open Spoken and allow it again. Spoken › Settings › Permissions shows which permission is missing.
Builds signed with a Developer ID will keep these permissions across updates.
The library format is unchanged. Builds 9 and newer can receive this update.
## Fresh installation
Download the DMG, drag **Spoken** to **Applications**, eject the DMG, then open Spoken from Applications. This is the release app, not Spoken Dev. The test target is an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 15 or newer.
This test build is **ad-hoc signed, not Developer ID signed or notarized**. macOS may require **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway** on first launch. In-app update archives are authenticated with Sparkle's EdDSA signature.
## Validation and limitations
The automated regression suite and the packaged artifact are checked before publication. MP4 import was checked with audio-only and video MP4 files, and the MCP response sizes were measured on the reference Mac. Known open items: calendars cannot yet be disconnected in Settings (KON-254), floating glass panels are hard to read on Macs without a notch (KON-255), and Models & Providers clips its details in a narrow window (KON-256). The Spoken Library remains local and unencrypted.

# Spoken 0.2.8 — Test Build 22
A new look, a calmer notch, a floating transcript player, calendar meetings that offer to record, and reliable echo removal on speaker calls.
## Changes
- **New design.** Spoken is now black and white, dark first, with an accent you choose in Settings › General › Appearance (none, a preset or your own color) and System, Light or Dark appearance. Buttons follow one clear order of importance instead of the system blue everywhere. - **Notch.** Dictation opens one compact panel: time beside the notch, the target app, a wave and the mode below. Meetings show their header beside the notch and the content below it; the small recording indicator sits right next to the notch. Screenshot notes and the "Still in the meeting?" reminder appear inside the recording. - **Microphones.** Dictation and meetings each have their own microphone choice, both "Like macOS" by default. Virtual inputs of meeting apps such as Teams or Zoom are no longer offered. - **Calendar.** Settings › Meetings › Calendar shows your calendars grouped by account and the meetings of each day. When a meeting with other people starts, Spoken opens New Meeting with that event chosen; nothing records until you press Start. The event is picked from a calendar button inside the title field, and invited people show as "First Last". - **Transcript.** A floating player at the bottom with a zoomable speaker timeline: pinch to zoom, swipe to move, click to jump. A pencil edits one passage in place; the speaker name reassigns one passage, with Undo. - **Speaker calls.** When a call plays through the Mac's speakers, the other side's echo is removed from your microphone far more reliably, and playback no longer amplifies it into a hall. Older meetings improve after "Speaker neu erkennen" or a new transcription. - **Fixes.** Very quiet microphones are no longer treated as silence. Settings hover no longer flashes, and choice fields keep their arrows at the right edge.

This test build is **ad-hoc signed, not Developer ID signed or notarized**. macOS may require **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway** on first launch. In-app update archives are authenticated with Sparkle's EdDSA signature.
## Validation and limitations

The new design, notch panels, microphone choice, calendar settings and meeting offer, transcript player and echo removal were checked on the reference Mac; echo removal was measured on a recorded Teams call on speakers. Known open items: the panel after a meeting does not yet have the new design everywhere (KON-247); live waves move little with a quiet MacBook microphone and show the other side on speaker calls (KON-251, KON-253); attendees cannot yet be sorted by their answer (KON-252). # Spoken 0.2.7 — Test Build 21
Cleaner meeting transcripts, echo removal and cheaper cloud transcription.
## Changes
- **Whole sentences per speaker.** Words from the microphone and the system audio were interleaved by time, so a short "yes" from the other side cut a sentence into one-word lines. Each person's sentence now stays together. Existing meetings improve when they are transcribed or their speakers detected again. - **Echo removal.** When a call plays through speakers, the other side's voice is removed from the microphone track before speakers are detected and the audio is transcribed. Spoken mutes only short blocks that repeat the system audio and keeps blocks where you talk at the same time. The recording itself never changes. With headphones nothing changes. - **Cloud transcription with separate tracks.** A provider on the internet, such as OpenAI or Groq, receives microphone and system audio as separate tracks, and only the speech of each, as compressed M4A: about 14 MB per hour of speech instead of 230 MB. Two tracks no longer cost twice the meeting. Servers on this Mac or your network still receive WAV. - **Transcript information.** The (i) button on a transcript shows the provider, whether it ran on this Mac or in the cloud, the model, the language and the speakers per track. - **Fixes.** Codex connects to the Spoken MCP server again. A failed re-transcription, for example when a provider has no credits left, can be dismissed with "Verwerfen"; the earlier transcript stays. The speaker review keeps its "Weiter" button visible.

Re-transcription with whole sentences, cloud transcription through Groq, the speaker review and the transcript information were checked on the reference Mac. Echo removal was measured on recorded speaker calls. Cloud transcription through OpenAI itself was not run for this build. # Spoken 0.2.6 — Test Build 20
A smooth notch overlay, area screenshots, calendar suggestions and more on-device models.
## Changes
- **Smooth notch overlay.** Meeting recording, dictation and the standby hint grow out of the notch as one shape and shrink back into it. Hovering opens the compact view, a click opens the controls. Two causes of stutter were measured and removed: the recording state was republished for every audio buffer, and the menu bar menu asked macOS about Apple Intelligence on every redraw. - **Area screenshots.** During a meeting, ⌥⇧A (or the dashed-square button in the overlay) opens the macOS selection: drag an area, press Space to pick a window, Escape cancels. ⌥⇧S still captures the whole screen. Both shortcuts are on by default and can be changed in Settings › Shortcuts. Closing the note card with X or Escape now discards that screenshot; "Ohne Notiz" keeps it. - **Calendar suggestions.** In Settings › Meetings › Calendar, allow access and choose the calendars to use. When a recording starts, Spoken proposes the title and invitees of the current or next calendar event; you can pick another event or edit both. Spoken only reads calendars added to macOS. - **On-device models.** More built-in speech models are available under Models & Providers, including Apple Speech for a fixed language. Apple's on-device text model can clean up short dictations; meeting summaries still need a text provider. - **Agents.** Per agent, you can allow setting changes and project creation. Every request is shown in Spoken for your approval. - **Fixes.** Discarding a new recording moves its meeting to the Trash instead of leaving it empty. Settings buttons in the recording overlay open Settings even when the main window is closed.
## Update an existing installation
In **Spoken**, choose **Check for Updates…**. Download and install the update, then allow Spoken to restart. The installed version should be **0.2.6 (20)**. Finish any recording or dictation first.
### If something stops working after the update

Spoken › Settings › Permissions shows which permission is missing.
Builds signed with a Developer ID will keep these permissions across updates.
The library is migrated once on first launch to store calendar context with meetings. Builds 9 and newer can receive this update.
## Fresh installation
Download the DMG, drag **Spoken** to **Applications**, eject the DMG, then open Spoken from Applications. This is the release app, not Spoken Dev. The test target is an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 15 or newer.
This test build is **ad-hoc signed, not Developer ID signed or notarized**. macOS may require **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway** on first launch. In-app update archives are authenticated with Sparkle's EdDSA signature.
## Validation and limitations
The automated regression suite and the packaged artifact are checked before publication. Overlay smoothness, area screenshots, calendar suggestions and an approved agent setting change were checked on the reference Mac. Known open items: an echo of the other side can appear in the microphone track when a call plays through speakers (KON-226); marking up screenshots in a call is not available yet (KON-241). The Spoken Library remains local and unencrypted.

# Spoken 0.2.5 — Test Build 19
Optional OpenAI API transcription, clearer model lists, and visible meeting processing steps.
## Changes
- **Optional speech API.** Add an OpenAI connection in Settings › Models & Providers with your own API key, then choose it separately for Dictation or Meetings. Built-in Parakeet remains the default and needs no API account. Spoken labels the processing location before audio is sent. Cloud use is explicit; sensitive projects require a separate allowance. - **Meeting models.** `whisper-1` can return word timestamps for local speaker matching. Text-only transcription models such as `gpt-transcribe` are offered for dictation, not for meetings. Spoken retains the original meeting audio if transcription fails. - **Stable route and provenance.** A meeting stores the exact provider profile and model used. If the selected connection, model, or sensitive-project permission changes during a long job, Spoken stops before another audio chunk is uploaded; retry after checking the settings. - **Provider models.** Search and filter a provider's reported models by text, vision, transcription, speech, image, embeddings, or enabled state. The list distinguishes reported facts, shared-list information, and name guesses. Its menu can set capabilities for an unusual model and control sensitive project access. - **Meeting progress.** The processing panel shows the current step, progress, and route. Failed transcription no longer loops into speaker review.
## Update an existing installation
In **Spoken**, choose **Check for Updates…**. Download and install the update, then allow Spoken to restart. The installed version should be **0.2.5 (19)**. Finish any recording or dictation first, and save pending document edits when asked. Existing provider and library settings remain in place; this build does not add a library migration.
Builds 9 and newer can receive this update. Older pre-library builds remain excluded from this update channel. OpenAI is optional and requires your own API key; Spoken does not use a ChatGPT account sign-in.
## Fresh installation
Download the DMG, drag **Spoken** to **Applications**, eject the DMG, then open Spoken from Applications. This is the release app, not Spoken Dev. The test target is an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 15 or newer.
This test build is **ad-hoc signed, not Developer ID signed or notarized**. macOS may require **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway** on first launch. Permissions may need to be granted again. In-app update archives are authenticated with Sparkle's EdDSA signature.
## Validation and limitations
The automated regression suite and packaged artifact are checked before publication. One consented synthetic German meeting sample was transcribed through OpenAI `whisper-1`; it does not establish quality or cost for long meetings. The full curated audio model catalog and broader evaluation remain follow-up work. The Spoken Library remains local and unencrypted.

# Spoken 0.2.4 — Test Build 18
One catalog for all flows, and sensitive projects that stay on the models you allow.
## Changes
- **Flow catalog.** Settings › Flows lists every flow with the number of projects using it. Flows are shared: edit one there and it changes in every project that uses it; duplicate it for a variant. Each project keeps its own output language, model and preselection, and uses up to ten flows. On a project page, **Add Flow** picks a catalog flow or writes a new one, which lands in the catalog. **New Project** lets you check the flows it starts with. Your existing flows are merged on the first start: identical flows become one catalog flow. - **Sensitive projects.** Each provider has **Allow for sensitive projects**. Local providers start allowed; Enterprise and Cloud only once you switch it on. Right-click a model to decide for it alone; Ollama cloud models always need their own allowance. Settings › Flows has a **Default model for sensitive projects**. A flow a sensitive project may not run shows a warning, cannot be started or checked after a meeting, and appears in the bell with every way to fix it. Dictation modes show whether their text leaves the Mac. - **Agents.** Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Exxperts can each be added once; Custom as often as needed. Profiles can be removed. - **Right-click to delete** a dictation mode, a provider or an agent in Settings.
## Update an existing installation
In **Spoken**, choose **Check for Updates…**, or use the sidebar update action when it appears. Download, install and allow Spoken to restart. The installed version afterwards should be **0.2.4 (18)**. Finish any recording or dictation before installing, and save pending document edits when asked.
On the first start the library is changed for the flow catalog. Spoken copies it to `backups/` inside the library first; the copy is deleted after 14 days or when you delete anything permanently. **Restart connected agents** (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Exxperts) afterwards so they read flows in the new format.
If a project is marked sensitive and its flows use an Enterprise or Cloud provider, those flows stop until you allow the provider or choose another model. The bell lists them.
Builds 9 and newer can receive this update. Older pre-library builds remain excluded from this update channel.
## Fresh installation
Download the DMG, drag **Spoken** to **Applications**, eject the DMG, then open Spoken from Applications. This is the release app, not Spoken Dev. Requires an Apple Silicon Mac; macOS 15 or newer is the supported test target.
This test build is **ad-hoc signed, not Developer ID signed or notarized**. macOS may require **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway** on first launch. Permissions may need to be granted again. In-app update archives are authenticated with Sparkle's EdDSA signature.
## Validation and limitations
The automated regression suite and packaged artifact are checked before publication. The library migration was tested on a copy of a real library. The library remains local and unencrypted.

# Spoken 0.2.3 — Test Build 17
Own dictation modes, a project page and one place for everything that needs attention.
## Changes
- **Your own dictation modes.** Settings › Dictation › Modes lists Raw and your modes. Create, rename, edit and delete them; each can use its own provider and model, and **Test** runs a mode on a spoken sample without inserting anything. Clean and Concise keep your prompts, **To English** is new, and Structured is gone (a shortcut that used it switches to Raw). The dictation history shows which mode each entry used. - **Project page.** Clicking a project shows two cards: its **About** text, written in Markdown and shown formatted, and its **flows** as a graph. It fits a split view too. Each result says whether its document exists for the chosen meeting: click to open it, or to create it. The sidebar lists only the meetings under a project, and new projects ask what they are about instead of creating a README. Agents see the About text. - **Needs attention.** A bell at the top right of the window lists what is misconfigured — a flow using a deleted provider, a provider that can't be reached, a dictation mode that can't run — and each entry jumps to where it is fixed. The menu bar shows "… need attention" only when something does. - **Flows.** After a meeting every flow of the project is offered; "Preselect after meetings" decides which start checked. The flow editor names its default model and lists a provider's models as soon as it is picked.
## Update an existing installation
In **Spoken**, choose **Check for Updates…**, or use the sidebar update action when it appears. Download, install and allow Spoken to restart. The installed version afterwards should be **0.2.3 (17)**. Finish any recording or dictation before installing, and save pending document edits when asked.
Builds 9 and newer can receive this update. Existing library content is preserved. Older pre-library builds remain excluded from this update channel.

# Spoken 0.2.2 — Test Build 16
A setup, dictation and agent update for the Spoken 0.2 workbench.
## Changes
- New first-launch setup in four steps in the main window: permissions in one list with explanations, the built-in speech model, a first dictation from the menu bar, and a summary. A Get Started checklist in the sidebar covers the optional next steps: connect an agent, record a meeting, add text and screenshot models. - Added **Exxperts** as an agent client. Spoken writes its connector with the profile's key directly into Exxperts' MCP configuration, never through the clipboard. - Clean, Concise and Structured no longer lose a dictation when no text provider is set up or the provider fails. The raw text is inserted and an orange notice says why, with a button to the provider settings. Cleanup gives up after 60 seconds without any response instead of ten minutes, and cancelling keeps the dictation and its audio in the history. - Dictation errors and the transcript preview grow out of the notch instead of hiding behind it. - The speech model starts loading as soon as a dictation starts, so the first dictation after a pause is faster. - A tidier menu bar menu: meeting recording on its own, then the last dictation, Dictation Mode and Dictation Options. "Nothing heard" explains how the shortcut works.

# Spoken 0.2.1 — Test Build 15
A security and reliability update for the Spoken 0.2 workbench.
## Changes
- Secured Markdown and diagram rendering against injected scripts and unwanted network requests. Diagrams, timestamp links and native document actions remain available. - Kept the original dictation when text cleanup fails. Retry Cleanup uses the same captured text; Insert Raw explicitly inserts the original transcript. Recovery updates the existing history entry rather than creating duplicates. - Fixed **Spoken beenden** in the screen-recording permission step: the wizard closes before the normal app quit request. Recording and unsaved-document protections remain active; forced termination is not used. - Added Back navigation in setup and an explicit already-allowed permission screen when reviewing previous steps. Visible permission screens refresh their status while Spoken is active.
